subject.title: message tool: Feishu send action polluted by poll schema/guard prevents file send

question: For plain `message.send`, should OpenClaw hide poll content fields from send-capable schemas, strip accidental poll fields at runtime, or keep rejecting content-bearing poll fields as explicit poll intent?
rationale: The remaining behavior affects the model-facing message tool contract across multiple channels, and changing it requires deciding whether send reliability or strict poll-intent validation wins when a model supplies contradictory fields.

options.title: Action-scope poll fields
options.body: Expose poll creation fields only for poll actions or channel-specific poll tools so ordinary sends cannot inherit them from the shared schema.

options.title: Strip on send
options.body: Treat `action="send"` as authoritative and drop poll creation fields before delivery, improving send reliability but potentially hiding callers that meant to create a poll.

options.title: Keep strict guard
options.body: Continue rejecting content-bearing poll fields on send and require stronger live evidence before changing the shared tool contract.

recommendation.title: Action-scope poll fields
recommendation.body: Expose poll creation fields only for poll actions or channel-specific poll tools so ordinary sends cannot inherit them from the shared schema.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged poll gating and schema-consistency history is the strongest signal for the shared send/poll contract boundary.
